title: Findings and Follow-up Actions on National Service Training Death
what_it_is: Findings and Follow-up Actions on National Service Training Death

sections.label: COI findings to Armed Forces Council
sections.summary: The COI completed its investigations and presents its findings as submitted to the Armed Forces Council.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The COI has completed its investigations and, in this Statement, I will present the findings of the COI as submitted to the Armed Forces Council (AFC).

sections.label: Pang injured in SSPH maintenance
sections.summary: On 19 January 2019, CFC(NS) Pang was injured during SSPH maintenance in Exercise Thunder Warrior, caught between the flick rammer and slew ring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: On 19 January 2019 at about 1900 hrs, CFC(NS) Pang sustained an injury while carrying out maintenance work on a Singapore Self-Propelled Howitzer (SSPH) involved in Exercise Thunder Warrior.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: CFC(NS) Pang was assisting in maintenance work in the SSPH when the gun barrel was lowered and he was caught between the flick rammer and the slew ring of the SSPH turret".

sections.label: Pang's death and maintenance chronology
sections.summary: CFC(NS) Pang died from severe sepsis from chest and abdominal injuries; the COI established a chronology, including his response to the gun detachment commander's call.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: CFC(NS) Pang died from severe sepsis arising from his severe chest and abdominal injuries as a result of being trapped between the flick rammer and the slew ring in the SSPH." The COI next established a detailed chronology of events leading to the injury and subsequent death of CFC(NS) Pang.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: On 19 January, CFC(NS) Pang had responded to the call from the gun detachment commander, the gun detachment commander was a 3SG NSman, for assistance to conduct corrective maintenance on his SSPH gun.

sections.label: ME-Tech's warning to Pang
sections.summary: The ME-Tech told CFC(NS) Pang in Mandarin and English that the gun barrel would move to standby and to move closer or to safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Based on the COI's findings, the ME-Tech informed CFC(NS) Pang in a mix of Mandarin and English that the gun barrel was going to be moved to the standby position and told CFC(NS) Pang to move either closer to him or to a safe position.

sections.label: COI opinion on panic and E-stop
sections.summary: The COI opined that the ME-Tech and GC panicked and acted irrationally instead of activating the Emergency Stop buttons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: As the gun barrel made contact with CFC(NS) Pang, the COI opined that instead of activating the Emergency Stop (E-stop) buttons, both the ME-Tech and the GC panicked, and acted irrationally.

sections.label: COI precipitating cause of incident
sections.summary: The COI opined the precipitating cause was lowering the gun barrel without ensuring everyone was in safe positions, with Pang in the barrel's path.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI opined that "the precipitating cause of the incident was due to the lowering of the gun barrel without ensuring that everyone was in their safe positions: (a) CFC(NS) Pang was standing in the path of the moving barrel and not in a safe position prior to the gun barrel being moved.

sections.label: COI findings on Pang's death
sections.summary: The COI found no foul play or deliberate acts, attributing the incident to lapses of the GC, ME-Tech and CFC(NS) Pang.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In their state of panic when the flick rammer hit CFC(NS) Pang, both the ME-Tech and the GC acted irrationally instead of activating the E-stop buttons." The COI found "no evidence indicating that CFC(NS) Pang’s death involved foul play or was caused by any deliberate acts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: However, the COI found that the incident was due to the lapses of all the servicemen who were in the gun at the time of the incident – the GC, the ME-Tech and CFC(NS) Pang".

sections.label: COI on medical care and causes
sections.summary: The COI found post-incident medical care adequate but improvable, and the direct causes of death preventable with safety compliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: On the post-incident medical care, the COI is of the opinion that in view of the extenuating circumstances caused by the distance and the availability of the helicopter, the medical care provided was adequate but can be improved.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Members of this House, I have presented the COI's findings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is sad but undeniable that the direct causes determined by the COI that resulted in the death of CFC(NS) Pang were preventable had there been compliance to safety rules.

sections.label: GC and safe position
sections.summary: The COI states the incident would not have happened if the GC had ensured CFC(NS) Pang was in a safe position.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If the GC had ensured that CFC(NS) Pang was in a safe position before activating the gun barrel to standby position, the incident would not have happened.

sections.label: COI safety culture recommendation
sections.summary: The COI recommended enhancing safety culture by having all SAF servicemen, especially NSmen, take personal ownership of safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI proposed the following recommendations aimed at preventing similar incidents in the future and enhancing the safety system, which I report in full. "(a) Enhance safety culture by ensuring that all Servicemen of the SAF and especially National Servicemen (NSmen) take personal ownership of safety.

sections.label: Risk assessment and near misses
sections.summary: The COI recommended more comprehensive risk assessment for high-risk activities and reporting and archiving of all near misses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: A more comprehensive risk assessment for high-risk activities should be conducted, and all near misses must be reported and archived.

sections.label: TSR education and safety officer
sections.summary: The COI recommended continued TSR education in quarterly Army Safety Seminars and a safety officer during peacetime live firing exercises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: There should be continued education on compliance with the TSR and this should be incorporated into the quarterly Army Safety Seminars.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: There could also be a safety officer appointed during peacetime live firing exercises to oversee safety and further develop the Safety Management Plan with regard to maintenance work and the maintenance crew's interaction with the gun crew.

sections.label: COI findings and ERPSS report
sections.summary: A guideline on managing remains of demised servicemen on overseas exercises should be drawn up, and the ERPSS agrees with the COI's findings and recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: A reference guideline should be drawn up with details on the protocol for the management of the remains of the demised serviceman on overseas exercises." I have concluded presenting the COI's findings and now turn to the External Review Panel on SAF Safety's (ERPSS') written report on the COI's findings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The ERPSS agrees with the COI's findings on the incident, and supports the proposed recommendations raised by the COI to prevent a similar incident from occurring.

sections.label: SAF Inspector-General's Office
sections.summary: The SAF Inspector-General's Office, set up in end February after the incident, will ensure the recommendations are followed through.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The SAF Inspector-General's Office (IGO) set up in end February this year after this incident will ensure that the recommendations are followed through.

sections.label: Annual soldier safety awareness test
sections.summary: All soldiers will be required to take a safety awareness test annually, which commanders and trainers now take.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: (d) All soldiers will be required to take a safety awareness test annually, which commanders and trainers now take.

sections.label: SIB investigation and Chief Military Prosecutor
sections.summary: The SIB has nearly completed its investigations and will report directly to the Chief Military Prosecutor, a senior legal officer deployed to MINDEF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The SIB has nearly completed its investigations and will report directly to the Chief Military Prosecutor, who is a senior legal officer deployed to MINDEF by the Legal Service Commission headed by the Chief Justice.

sections.label: SAF updates CFC Pang's family
sections.summary: The SAF has updated CFC(NS) Pang's family on the COI's findings and actions taken, and MINDEF and the SAF will continue helping his family.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The SAF has updated CFC(NS) Pang's family on the COI's findings and the actions taken to deal with the lapses and prevent recurrences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: MINDEF and the SAF will continue to do all we can to help his family through this difficult period.

sections.label: Military Court, SIB prosecutorial factors
sections.summary: For prosecutorial purposes, the Military Court and SIB will hear other findings and decide factors, but there was no indication language was an issue within the turret.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And as I have said, separately, for prosecutorial purposes, the Military Court, the SIB and, if they decide to charge, the Military Court, will hear other findings and decide all these factors that Members of this House and others in the public might bring up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But there was no indication that communication, because of language, was an issue within the turret.

sections.label: Human error by three people
sections.summary: The incident did not arise from a technical fault but from human error of three people at the site.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One of the things that is clear is that the incident did not arise due to a technical fault, but really due to human error of three different people who were at the site.

sections.label: Three ignored safety rules
sections.summary: All three in the cabin ignored safety rules, with no operational reasons, saying they wanted to get on with it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If anyone of the three in the cabin, anyone of them, has followed the rules, this would not have happened.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is a fact that all three ignored the safety rules.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: No, there were no operational reasons why they did not comply with it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The reason given was that they wanted to get on with it.

sections.label: First incident in 15 years
sections.summary: This is the first such incident in 15 years of operation, and it is not widespread.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And I think the sense is, and this is not widespread because this is a first such incident, when this happened, I asked how many accidents have there occurred before, major injuries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This is the first for 15 years of operation.

sections.label: Waiting for gun to lower
sections.summary: Lowering and parking the gun as the safety manual says takes no more than 10 seconds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But in this instance, it just meant a few seconds of waiting before the gun was lowered – and we measured it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I think it does not take more than 10 seconds for the gun to be lowered, to be parked, as the safety manual says, to begin your work.
